item.title: Paraguay crash Moriyasu's Japan farewell party
item.description: Juan Caceres (L) volleyed Paragiuay ahead after just 64 seconds (Roslan RAHMAN) Hajime Moriyasu's tenure as Japan manager came to a disappointing end on Tuesday as his team were beaten 2-1 by Paraguay in an international friendly in Singapore. The defeat came just three days after the Samurai Blue upset Brazil 3-2. Juan Caceres volleyed the South Americans ahead after just 64 seconds, and captain Gustavo Gomez headed in Paraguay's second late in the first half, both from Diego Gomez corners. Shio Fukuda narrowed the deficit with a late header, but Japan were unable to find an equaliser to cap Moriyasu's eight-year reign with a positive result. The 58-year-old will be replaced by Japan's under-23 coach Go Oiwa. The crowd of 19,826 had barely settled into their seats at the National Stadium when Paraguay delivered the opening blow. An unmarked Caceres crashed a fierce volley past goalkeeper Zion Suzuki from Diego Gomez's corner. Paraguay's physical approach made it difficult for Japan to create opportunities. The Samurai Blue could have had a penalty late in the first half after Kodai Sano's effort struck the arm of Omar Alderete in the Paraguay box. But Thai referee Mongkolchai Pechsri decided not to overturn his original decision despite a VAR intervention. Japan's frustration was compounded when Paraguay added a second from another Diego Gomez corner as Gustavo Gomez met his delivery with a powerful header. Japan were much improved after the interval but they were unable to break down the stubborn Paraguay defence as goalkeeper Orlando Gill denied Kodai Sano from close range and substitutes Koki Ogawa and Takefusa Kubo also missed chances. However, they finally pulled a goal back in the 84th minute. Gill palmed away a Kubo free-kick but Fukuda got to the loose ball first and lobbed a header into the far corner of the net. It proved to be just a consolation, however, and Moriyasu's final game as Japan manager ended in defeat. str/jhe/bc

item.title: York City player pleads not guilty over alleged punch of Rochdale fan
item.description: Hiram Boateng allegedly hit a Rochdale AFC supporter after a pitch invasion by fans in April [Getty Images] A York City FC player has appeared in court after allegedly punching a Rochdale AFC supporter during a pitch invasion. Hiram Boateng, 30, of Leeds, pleaded not guilty at Manchester Magistrates' Court on Monday to using threatening, abusive or insulting behaviour with intent to cause fear of, or provoke, unlawful violence. The charge relates to an incident involving fans who entered the pitch during the final-day match between the two sides at the Crown Oil Arena on 25 April. York City FC said it was "aware of developments" following the incident and added Boateng, whose trial is due to begin on 23 June 2027, "maintains the full support of everyone at York City". Rochdale supporters entered the pitch during the match after believing their side had secured the National League title. The alleged incident happened during a second pitch invasion later in the game. A spokesperson for York City FC said: "We are aware of developments regarding the incident involving Hiram Boateng during the game against Rochdale in April. "We are continuing to work with him and all the appropriate authorities to address this and to understand the circumstances that led to this. "Hiram maintains the full support of everyone at York City and is a much-valued member of the squad, both on and off the pitch." Boateng is charged with a Section 4 public order offence which carries a maximum sentence of six months in prison. item.title: Joe Hart: Liverpool must have ‘grown-up conversations’ over dilemma with ‘adopted Scouser’
item.description: Joe Hart: Liverpool must have ‘grown-up conversations’ over dilemma with ‘adopted Scouser’ Joe Hart has said that Liverpool need to have ‘grown-up conversations’ with Alisson Becker regarding his contract situation at Anfield. The Reds’ long-serving number 1 – who turned 34 in October – has just over seven months remaining on his existing deal, and he recently expressed his desire to remain on Merseyside beyond next summer. The Brazilian’s agent Ze Maria has indicated that ‘preliminary talks’ are underway with LFC rearding a possible extension for the goalkeeper, who produced an outstanding performance in the win at Crystal Palace prior to the international break. Hart has his say on Alisson’s contract situation Speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate , Hart believes that Alisson will be offered a new contract, but the length of those terms could pose a tricky dilemma for the relevant parties. The ex-England goalkeeper said: “In his eyes there’s still a lot of legs in him, so you’ve gotta be really careful. I imagine Liverpool will offer him a new contract, but they can’t offer him a one-year contract. Can they offer him two (years) with everything that’s gone on, and then you talk about balancing wages? “I think there needs to be some grown-up conversations behind the scenes. Are Liverpool capable of having those conversations with Alisson? He’s the kind of guy who wants Liverpool to do well. “He’s an adopted Scouser and I love that about him. He’s one of the best to play in the Premier League , but are Liverpool capable of having those grown-up conversations with him? It felt a bit fractious with him towards the end of last season and potentially he was looking elsewhere.” (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? He’s currently on £250,000 per week, a figure exceeded by just six of his teammates ( Capology ), so any renewal would either see the club commit to a significant financial outlay, or the goalkeeper accepting lower wages to remain at Anfield for at least one more year. Hart’s point about the length of any new contract offer is pertinent. Do Liverpool offer just 12 months and find themselves back at this juncture again next autumn? Do they agree to pay him a high salary for two more seasons, at the end of which he’d be nearly 37? The Reds have Giorgi Mamardashvili and (from next summer) Lucca Brughmans as prospective long-term successors to Alisson, but such is the world-class brilliance of our number 1 that keeping him for as long as possible seems a no-brainer. item.title: Schalke deliver positive update on fitness of Sylla, Gosens and Gantenbein
item.description: Schalke deliver positive update on fitness of Sylla, Gosens and Gantenbein Ahead of the Bundesliga's return, FC Schalke 04 have issued a positive update regarding several members of Miron Muslic's personnel. Moussa Sylla and Adrian Gantenbein — back on the pitch since last week — took part in the full training session today, Tuesday. Meanwhile, both Janik Bachmann and Robin Gosens were also able to join in parts of team training again after layoffs. Gosens was of particular concern before the international break, hobbling off with a heavily strapped knee in their 2-1 loss to Hoffenheim. However, it appears any fears regarding a long-term layoff have been put to bed for the 32-year-old wing-back. Sylla also comes as a welcome return for the Gelsenkirchen club given Muslic's men have only managed 5 goals in 9 Bundesliga games.

item.title: Who could replace Mauricio Pochettino? Candidates for next USMNT coach
item.description: CINCINNATI — Mauricio Pochettino has reached the end of the road as U.S. men's national team head coach. Pochettino's final game in charge will come on on Tuesday, Nov. 17, as the USMNT faces Haiti in the second leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal. Pochettino will depart after the game to take over Manchester United . The final whistle at TQL Stadium on Tuesday will signal the official start of the USMNT's coaching search. In terms of timing, Pochettino's departure was pretty ideal. Aside from a December friendly against Jamaica that falls outside of a FIFA window, the U.S. won't (barring a stunning six-goal turnaround against Haiti) be in action until March's Nations League Finals. That should give the federation plenty of time to sound out candidates and bring in a coach with some time to spare before March. Here are some of the top candidates U.S. Soccer will likely be considering: Pep Guardiola - Unattached The legendary former Barcelona, Bayern and Man City boss is seen as something of a dream candidate, but that dream became a little closer to reality last week amid multiple reports that U.S. Soccer would target the Spaniard. The Telegraph poured some cold water on that idea over the weekend, reporting that Guardiola is set to reject any approach from U.S. Soccer as he is committed to taking a year off after leaving Man City over the summer. Steve Cherundolo - USMNT U-23 Cherundolo was always seen as one of the top contenders for the job, and that status was confirmed when U.S. Soccer announced he would take charge of the USMNT's December camp and match against Jamaica. The longtime USMNT defender will get the first crack to coach the team in its post-Pochettino era. He could very well take the job and run with it given his previous success as a MLS coach, experience playing and coaching abroad, and coaching connections to U.S. Soccer. B.J. Callaghan - Nashville SC Callaghan has emerged as one of the top candidates thanks to his work with Nashville combined with previous USMNT experience. In his first full-time head coaching job, Callaghan has turned Nashville into a MLS powerhouse and led the club to a MLS-record haul of 77 points this season. The 45-year-old also worked as an assistant on Gregg Berhalter's staff, then took over as interim coach in 2023. He led the USMNT to victory in the 2023 Concacaf Nations League Finals and the semifinals of the 2023 Gold Cup. Pellegrino Matarazzo - Real Sociedad With Matarazzo and the USMNT, the question has been more about timing than whether there is mutual interest. The New Jersey native has said that he had talks with U.S. Soccer in 2024 over the role, which ultimately went to Pochettino. item.title: NBA to Host First-Ever ‘Culinary All-Stars’ With Guy Fieri & ‘Top Chef’ Winners
item.description: Culinary All-Stars - Culinary All-Stars (courtesy of the NBA) Food Network and Bravo favorites are teaming up with the NBA for a major culinary crossover during All-Star Weekend next year. Today, NBA Experiences presented by DoorDash announced the debut of Culinary All-Stars, an elevated food-and-basketball event set to take place ahead of the Castrol Rising Stars game during NBA All-Star 2027 in Phoenix. The event will take place on Friday, February 19, 2027, on the suite level at Mortgage Matchup Center, and bring together chefs, TV personalities, and basketball legends. Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives and Guy’s Grocery Games host Guy Fieri will make a special appearance along with former Phoenix Suns star and NBA player Shawn Marion. The lineup also features chefs from across the culinary TV landscape, including 2026 Top Chef winner Rhoda Magbitang, Top Chef alums Kwame Onwuachi and Maria Mazon, and Guy’s Grocery Games personality Aaron May, as well as James Beard Award-winning Arizona chefs Chris Bianco and René Andrade. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NBA Experiences (@nbaexperiences) Marion—who reality TV fans may also recognize from competing on Season 30 of The Amazing Race with fellow former Suns star Cedric Ceballos—is excited to return to his old stomping grounds for the event. “Phoenix has always been special to me, and I have so many great memories from my time with the Suns, so it’s exciting to be back for NBA All-Star 2027,” Marion said in a statement. “I’m looking forward to being part of Culinary All-Stars and bringing fans together through two things that have always been a big part of the NBA experience: great food and basketball.” Related Rhoda Magbitang Opens Up About Her 'Top Chef' Win and What's Next While Culinary All-Stars itself is an exclusive, in-person VIP hospitality event rather than a standalone TV broadcast, the Castrol Rising Stars game following the tasting event will stream live on Peacock . For fans looking to attend in person, Culinary All-Stars packages—which bundle admission to the chef-led tasting event with tickets to the Castrol Rising Stars game—are available through nbaexperiences.com/culinary-all-stars , along with add-on options for existing game ticket holders and VIP wine-tasting packages. Meanwhile, fans following along from home can also catch event highlights, exclusive chef content, and behind-the-scenes updates online and on social media via NBA Experiences’ official social accounts, including its Instagram page at @nbaexperiences . NBA All-Star 2027 takes place in Phoenix from Friday, February 19, through Sunday, February 21, 2027, with Castrol Rising Stars streaming Friday on Peacock, All-Star Saturday Night airing Saturday on NBC and Peacock, and the 76th NBA All-Star Game airing Sunday on NBC, Peacock, and Telemundo. item.title: Cubs trade target: Steven Kwan
item.description: Okay, so most of you didn’t like the idea of the Cubs trading for Jarren Duran, which I posted here Friday . So what about Cleveland Guardians outfielder Steven Kwan? Kwan is an excellent defensive outfielder. He’s got four Gold Gloves, though he didn’t win one in 2026. That wasn’t because he wasn’t good defensively — it’s because he split his time between left field and center field and didn’t play enough innings at either position to qualify. That wouldn’t be the case if the Cubs acquired him; he’d play left field full time, though he’s good enough in center that he could give Pete Crow-Armstrong an occasional day off from playing center. Kwan doesn’t have much power, though he did hit 14 home runs in 2024 and 11 in 2025. His best offensive talent is on-base ability. He drew 85 walks in 2026, which ranked seventh in the AL. Combined with a .282 BA, that gave him a .382 OBP, good for fourth-best in the AL. He was the Guardians’ leadoff hitter most of 2026 and obviously the Cubs wouldn’t need him to do that, but that on-base ability works no matter where he would be in the batting order. Also, he doesn’t strike out much, which would be a refreshing change from most hitters in the Cubs lineup. Would you trade Matt Shaw for Kwan? I’d think the Guardians would do that. Maybe that’s too much considering Kwan is just one year from free agency. Kwan made $7.725 million in 2026 and is arb-eligible. MLB Trade Rumors projects him at $11.3 million for 2027, which should be affordable even with the belt-tightening Cubs. Would you do it? Here are 17 minutes worth of Kwan highlights from 2026.

item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Jeff Nelson
item.description: BRONX, NY - OCTOBER 18: Pitcher Jeff Nelson #43 of the New York Yankees pitches during game 1 of the Major League Baseball World Series against the Florida Marlins on October 18, 2003 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, New York. The Marlins won 3-2. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeff Nelson was born in Baltimore and grew up in the area southwest of the city. He lettered in baseball and basketball at Catonsville High School, and despite standing six-foot-eight, he opted for the pitcher’s mound instead of the hardwood. After graduating from Catonsville, Nelson was selected by the Los Angeles Dodgers in the 1984 MLB Amateur Draft, setting in motion what would ultimately be a fruitful 15-year MLB career. Jeffrey Allan Nelson Born: November 17, 1966 (Baltimore, MD) Yankees Tenure: 1996-2000, 2003 The Dodgers used the big righty almost exclusively as a reliever in their farm system over the next few seasons before the Mariners selected him in the minor-league phase of the Rule 5 Draft in December 1986. With Seattle, success did not come immediately, as Nelson spent several more years working his way through the minor leagues. He finally reached Triple-A in 1991 and began the 1992 season with the Mariners’ top affiliate in Calgary. Just a few games into the season, Nelson received his first call to the majors. After his debut, Nelson quickly established himself as a major-league reliever, appearing in 66 games as a rookie in 1992 and 71 games the following season. He was particularly effective against right-handed hitters but struggled more against lefties. Then, in 1995, he put together what would be one of his best major league seasons. Using his devastating slider, Nelson went 7-3 with a 2.17 ERA over 78.2 innings while appearing in 62 games. The following offseason, he was included in a trade with Tino Martinez and Jim Mecir to the New York Yankees for Russ Davis and Sterling Hitchcock. This trade was a major win for the Yankees. Both Nelson and Martinez would become staples of the dynasty years. Nelson’s first season in pinstripes was 1996. Manager Joe Torre called on him 73 times and got 74.1 innings from the reliever, who posted a 4.36 ERA and struck out 91 batters during the regular season. Nelson elevated his game when it mattered most in the postseason. Facing the Braves in the World Series, he appeared in three games and tossed 4.1 scoreless innings, allowing just one hit while striking out five to help secure the Yankees’ first championship since 1978. Following the title, the Yankees added Mike Stanton in the offseason, who paired with Nelson to form one of the most feared setup duos of the era. Nelson set his career high in 1997, appearing in 77 games, a then-record for the Yankees. Nelson took seven losses on the season, but his ERA dropped to a very clean 2.86. item.title: DERBY GLORY FOR U16 AND U15 TEAMS
item.description: DERBY GLORY FOR U16 AND U15 TEAMS A weekend to remember, not just because of the results themselves, but because of what those results mean. Having already beaten Inter at Under 17 level, the Under-16s and Under-15s claimed derby victories of their own on Saturday and Sunday, both winning away against their Nerazzurri counterparts. The two victories had a lot in common , both in terms of how they unfolded and in what they mean for the development and growth of two ambitious and hardworking teams. Both the Under-16s ( 1-0 ) and Under-15s ( 2-0 ) kept clean sheets , while all three goalscorers (Santopaolo for Baldo's side, and Miglioranza and Massaro for Cresta's) scored their first goals of the season. That highlights another statistic that reflects the work being done every day at the PUMA House of Football: after eight league matches, 22 different players have already scored this season , 9 for the Under-16s and 13 for the Under-15s. There are so many contributing factors to the strong starts enjoyed by both teams, who now sit unbeaten at the top of their respective groups, the only undefeated sides in their respective Group B tables. The Under-16s have 20 points (six wins and two draws), conceding just two goals in eight matches. The Under-15s , meanwhile, sit on 22 points, having overtaken an Atalanta side which won its first seven matches. It has been an ideal start for two teams that came into the season with high expectations. These Under-16s, for example, have won two national titles in previous seasons, at Under-14 and Under-15 level, while the Under-15s also impressed during their earlier years in grassroots football. Both teams continue to make steady progress, with much of their strength and success coming from a mix of players who have spent their entire development journey with the Rossoneri, starting in the youngest age groups at the PUMA House of Football, and recent arrivals who have settled seamlessly into the close-knit established squads. item.title: Roma Star Remains in Two EPL Powerhouses’ Crosshairs
item.description: Roma Star Remains in Two EPL Powerhouses’ Crosshairs Manu Koné returned from injury before the break, and Roma are bracing for the likely offers for him coming from the Premier League again in January, in particular from Chelsea and Manchester United, La Gazzetta dello Sport informs. The Blues came reasonably close to acquiring him last summer, but Gian Piero Gasperini shut it down because it would have been too late to secure a top-notch replacement. They had offered €60M with two days to go in the window. The Giallorossi brass would have been content with the fee. Kone will have a similar valuation in January, but the timing and the structure of the proposal will be decisive. The gaffer might be more permissive if the sale led to the acquisition of the winger he’s been clamoring for. Jamie Gittens is one of his preferred options . The Red Devils should be in the race too. The midfielder has two and a half more years on his contract at a rather modest rate for his caliber, €3.2M annually. The Pensioners had offered him a lot more, and he would have gladly transferred. The Giallorossi would have to renew his contract and significantly improve his salary if they held on to him again. They are in a tricky spot with UEFA concerning the FFP parameters. A big sale would aid more than raising their payroll in that sense. Our Take on Roma and Koné Their midfield is obviously much more imposing with him, but it didn’t flounder when he was out, so perhaps his departure will have better chances in the next couple of windows, as they’d likely be able to sign a worthy substitute and another big weapon with the income.

item.title: ‘I’m equipped’: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander says he’s ready to do something now for first time since 2019
item.description: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images Shai Gilgeous-Alexander came into the season with two consecutive MVP award wins. The Oklahoma City Thunder superstar is one of the best players in the NBA, and we’re sure he has his sights set on making it three in three, even though it’s not as straightforward this time. However, Gilgeous-Alexander worked all summer to achieve one thing, and he says he is well equipped to do just that. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander says he is ready to play all 82 games this season The NBA is one of the most gruelling competitions in sports. Teams play multiple games every week, and the workload and travel involved takes its toll on everyone, even the best players. That leads to injuries, which force players to the sidelines. Gilgeous-Alexander won the MVP award last season, but he only managed to play 68 games in the regular season. The only time he has ever played all 82 games in a season was in his rookie year with the Los Angeles Clippers back in 2018-19. Now, the Canadian says he has worked all summer to replicate that, and he feels he is ready to do it for the Oklahoma City Thunder. When asked about workload concerns, Gilgeous-Alexander said in a press conference : “Not at all. I worked my b*** off in the summertime to be able to play all 82, and play whatever is needed to win an NBA championship. “That’s my goal, and that’s what I strive after, conditioning-wise, in the summertime, and I think I’m equipped to do so.” The Thunder have been ravaged by injuries this season, with Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren all ruled out until next year. That is why they haven’t been as good as the Spurs or the Lakers yet, but if Gilgeous-Alexander can manage to play all 82 games for the first time since 2019, the Thunder could go all the way. item.title: Beyond The Box Score: Expected
item.description: Yeah. Last week I had to go to the grocery store for two specific items: beef jerky and alcohol. The process of getting those items wasn’t difficult. The grocery store closest to my house is not that far and it’s a series of right turns to get there which meant it was a unmemorable, very routine effort to make the trip and stop at that location to get those items. The items were easy to get. It took about two minutes to walk in, collect them, and head to the front to pay and leave. Because there was alcohol involved I had to show my ID. I’ve always assumed that anyone in their 40s with kids has enough life absent in their eyes that identification proving you’re over 21 isn’t needed, but hey, the law is the law so whatever. However, as the cashier checks my date of birth, she remarks, “I have the same birthday”. There really isn’t a boilerplate response to a stranger telling you that you share the same date of birth so I just went with “well happy birthday four weeks ago” and figured that was it. But the guy bagging the groceries at the end of the lane asked what day our birthdays were. And when she responded he said “oh man that’s my birthday, too”. We kind of just stood there for a second. I mean, what are the odds that you’re mindlessly going about your day and knowingly run into someone with your birthday, let alone two other people, in a completely non-scripted, random interaction? The best part, though, was the grocery bagger guy jumped in with, “man, the Universe brought us all together to make sure this guy gets this beef jerky. I like that”. It was an absurd enough statement that we all had a decent laugh at it. And I’m sure you’re sitting here reading this and thinking, “this is stupid and not funny”, but it’s one of those moments that’s so unlikely to ever occur with a funny enough statement to add that, in the moment, you can’t help but laugh at the long odds of this sort of thing ever happening again. It was fun, totally unexpected occurrence. I enjoyed it. And from the list of not fun, expected occurrences that I did not enjoy, Missouri’s football team was wiped off the face of the Earth by Georgia on Saturday. Just a complete washout. Even the garbage time stats added in don’t make this look any better. When Missouri Has the Ball Missouri ended the game with a 51.7% success rate throwing the ball which…yes, that is what happened. But heading into the 4th quarter the passing success rate was 40%. Meanwhile, Missouri could find very little efficiency on the ground over the entire game. Unless Ahmad Hardy was running the ball, anyway. And even then he was at 42.9% over his seven carries. (Jim Franco/Times Union) Keegan Croucher, who began his varsity football career at Fonda-Fultonville in 2023 and now plays at Baylor School in Chattanooga, Tenn., has been rated as the No. 1 quarterback in the recruiting class of 2027 in the latest edition of the Rivals Top 300 recruiting rankings. Rivals lists Croucher as a five-star recruiting prospect and the No. 9 recruit overall in this year's senior class, in addition to his spot as the No. 1 quarterback. Croucher was considered among the top six quarterbacks in the class of 2027 in national recruiting lists published earlier this season. Baylor School running back David Gabriel Georges, a Tennessee commit, is rated the top running back in the class and No. 21 overall. The Red Raiders are coming off a 49-7 victory over Christ Presbyterian Academy in the Division II Class AAA state quarterfinals where Croucher threw for 298 yards and three touchdowns. The team competes Friday in state semifinal action against Briarcrest Christian. Head coach Mike Vrabel indicated Monday that making an external addition wasn’t currently the plan, backing quarterbacks Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton. However, reports suggest the Patriots could explore outside options during their bye week. Most likely, any addition would fill the No. 3 quarterback role, with DeVito and Morton expected to receive increased practice reps throughout the week. item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - SEPTEMBER 25: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers celebrates after hitting a solo home run in the second inning during the game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park on Friday, September 25, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Kavin Mistry/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Who could have guessed that with the signing of Kyle Tucker, it’d be Andy Pages ending the 2026 regular season as unequivocally the most impactful Dodger outfielder on both sides of the ball. Taking advantage of a rare playing time opportunity in this loaded Dodger squad a couple of seasons ago, Pages established himself as the team’s top center fielder in 2024—and ever since, his bat has seen a gradual progression, culminating in an All-Star campaign in 2026. Pages’ 2025 campaign had already been quite impressive, but what allowed him to take his game to a new level in 2026 was improved plate discipline. Never known for his patience at the plate, Pages opened the year with a 5.4 percent walk rate. This year that number improved to 8.5 percent, helping elevate his on-base percentage from .313 to .343, the main reason for this superior form. There is a chicken-and-egg question when it comes to Pages’ improved plate discipline, considering pitchers drastically decreased the zone rate against Pages, feeding him the fewest strikes he’s seen as a big leaguer. A 53.3 percent zone rate in 2025 decreased all the way to 45.5 percent this year. Adjusting to this new approach against him, Pages began to swing much less—his whiff rate remained similar, but the outfielder was more selective at the plate, and was rewarded for it. Pages’ production in the first half of the season was such that it earned him not only a starting nod as the NL’s center fielder in the All-Star Game, but he was the top vote-getter among NL outfielders with 2,158,664 votes.
